slides.title: Why not to leave EMI/RFI for band-limiting?
text: Why not to leave EMI/RFI for band-limiting?
You can saturate the amplifier – clipping.
You can create intermodulation products that fall into the passband.
No filter after the amplifier can remove the distortion products cleanly.
100 Ω + 100 pF input shunt gives 𝑓𝑐≈12𝜋𝑅𝐶≈16 MHz → great for RF, irrelevant for ECG.
ECG LPF at 40 Hz needs something like 39 kΩ + 100 nF → totally different scale.

slides.title: PGA – programmable gain amplifiers
text: A PGA (Programmable Gain Amplifier) is an amplifier whose gain can be changed electronically (usually by a microcontroller/FPGA via SPI/I²C or logic pins).
In biosignal front-ends it’s used so tiny signals (µV–mV) can be scaled to the ADC’s full input range without saturating, improving measurement quality.
Low gain when signals are large (startup, motion artifacts, etc.)
High gain when the signal is small, to use more of the ADC range.

slides.title: Keep analog minimal — but not zero
text: Keep analog minimal — but not zero
In theory, we could use a very high-resolution ADC (32-Bit) and do everything in the digital (discrete-time) domain.
We still need a small analog front end to:
Filter out EMI/RFI – MHz and GHz.
Amplify – allow ADC to use whole range efficiently.
Limit bandwidth before sampling (anti-aliasing) – so we process what is need.
Level shift – ADC can’t see negative part of signal.

slides.title: Oversampling helps, but it doesn’t remove the need for analog constraints
text: Oversampling helps, but it doesn’t remove the need for analog constraints
The sampling rate must be > 2× the highest frequency that reaches the ADC (after the analog front-end bandwidth limit).
If we push everything digital, we pay in data rate, storage, compute, and power.
So we aim for a balanced split:
Remove what is clearly non-physiological / interference early.
Preserve as much potentially informative variability as possible for DSP (what looks like “noise” can contain physiology).

slides.title: How do we make dB “absolute”?
text: We add a suffix that states the reference level. The decibel is still a ratio, but now the reference is fixed by convention:
dBm: reference power is 1 mW (so 0 dBm = 1 mW)
dBV: reference voltage is 1 V RMS (so 0 dBV = 1 Vrms)
dBFS (digital): reference is full scale – 0 dBFS
dB SPL (acoustics): sound pressure in air 20 µPa
dBu: reference voltage is 0.775 V RMS

slides.title: Patient protection from electronic
text: Isolation – prevents dangerous currents and ground-loop paths from reaching the patient-connected circuitry.
Leakage current – Even with isolation, tiny AC currents can ‘leak’ through capacitances.
Fault current – Fault current protection limits how much current can flow to the patient during abnormal events (single-fault, misconnection, transients).
